title: Products per Category as Comma-Separated List
description:
For each product category, list all product names as a single **comma-separated string**, aliased as `product_list`.

**Table: products**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| category | VARCHAR |
| price | DECIMAL |
| stock_quantity | INT |

Output columns: `category`, `product_list`. Order by `category`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, stock_quantity INT); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Laptop','Electronics',999.99,10),(2,'Phone','Electronics',699.99,25),(3,'Monitor','Electronics',349.99,15),(4,'Desk','Furniture',299.99,5),(5,'Chair','Furniture',149.99,8);
solution_sql: SELECT category, STRING_AGG(name, ', ' ORDER BY name) AS product_list FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY category

test_cases.description: Electronics: Laptop, Monitor, Phone; Furniture: Chair, Desk

hints: STRING_AGG(column, separator) concatenates values within a group.
Add ORDER BY inside STRING_AGG to get a deterministic order.
explanation: STRING_AGG concatenates column values within each GROUP BY group. The `ORDER BY name` inside STRING_AGG sorts the names alphabetically within each category before joining them.
